input.quote: 7. LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.
input.rationale: Section 7's heading promises "Indemnification of Contractor," but the section contains only liability caps (7(a)), a consequential-damages waiver (7(b)) and an attorneys' fees waiver (7(c)) — a full-text search for "indemn" returns only the heading, so no operative indemnity exists anywhere in the Agreement in either direction. That fails even the fallback: there is no Vendor IP indemnity, no defence obligation, and no remedy for third-party infringement claims. The 5(c) IP non-infringement warranty is not a substitute, because a warranty carries no duty to defend or to fund our costs, and any resulting claim would be squeezed into the 7(a) cap of fees paid (with 7(c) forcing us to bear our own attorneys' fees). The 7(a) cross-reference to "Contractor's obligations pursuant to Paragraph 9" appears to be a drafting error, since Paragraph 9 is Independent Contractor status, not an indemnity. We inserted the preferred Vendor indemnity (IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused disclosure of Confidential Information, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics as new 7(d), carved out of the Section 7 limitations, and conformed the heading. No Customer indemnity exists to narrow. A 3x annual fees super-cap on these obligations is available as a fallback.

proposal.summary: Insert a Contractor indemnity (IP infringement, breach of law, data/confidentiality incidents, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) as new Section 7(d), carved out of the liability limitations, and correct the section heading.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 7 is titled "Indemnification of Contractor" but contains no indemnity at all, so we have no protection against third-party IP or misconduct claims arising from RadialSpark's services; the 5(c) IP warranty alone does not cover our defence costs. We have added a standard Contractor indemnity with notice, control and cooperation mechanics, carved out of the Section 7 caps; if a cap is essential we can accept a super-cap of 3x annual fees on these obligations.

ops.oldText: 7. LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.

ops.text: (d) Contractor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (i) an allegation that the Services or Works infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (ii) Contractor's breach of applicable law; (iii) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Company's Confidential Information caused by Contractor; or (iv) Contractor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Company shall give Contractor prompt written notice of any such claim and reasonable cooperation at Contractor's expense, and Contractor shall have sole control of the defense and settlement, provided that no settlement imposing any liability or admission on Company shall be made without Company's prior written consent. Contractor's obligations under this Section 7(d) are not subject to the limitations set forth in Sections 7(a), 7(b) and 7(c).
